common_name: Cityline Vienna Hydrangea (Compact Pink-Purple Mophead Hydrangea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Cityline Vienna carries dense, rounded mophead trusses on a tidy, compact frame bred to resist flopping in wind and rain.

directions: Cityline Vienna is a compact bigleaf hydrangea bred for a dense, well-branched habit under 3 feet, carrying rounded mophead clusters that run from rosy pink to violet-purple depending on soil chemistry. As with other Cityline selections, sturdy stems hold the heavy flower heads upright through summer storms rather than sprawling outward as many older cultivars do. Aluminum sulfate applied around the root zone in acidic soil pushes color toward blue-purple, while garden lime keeps tones warmer and pinker. Keep the root zone evenly moist and mulched in partial shade, and limit pruning to dead-wood removal so next year's old-wood buds are not lost.
sources: North Carolina State Extension — Compact Bigleaf Hydrangea Series

common_name: Let's Dance Moonlight Hydrangea (Cold-Hardy Reblooming Mophead Hydrangea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Let's Dance Moonlight was bred for unusually heavy bud set on new wood, giving strong rebloom even where winterkill removes most of the old-wood buds.

directions: Let's Dance Moonlight produces oversized mophead flower clusters on a Let's Dance-series plant selected specifically for cold hardiness, setting flower buds abundantly on new growth so a hard winter that kills old wood still leaves a full season of bloom. Plant in consistently moist, humus-rich soil in full sun to partial shade, giving afternoon shade where summers run hot. Flower color follows the usual macrophylla pattern, shifting toward blue-purple in acidic soil with added aluminum sulfate and toward pink as soil pH rises with garden lime. Prune minimally, removing only dead or damaged wood right after flowering, since old-wood buds that survive winter still contribute significant early-season bloom alongside the reliable new-wood flush.
sources: Proven Winners ColorChoice Shrubs — Let's Dance Hydrangea Series

common_name: Wedding Gown Hydrangea (Double White Reblooming Lacecap Hydrangea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in morning sun with afternoon shade; Wedding Gown's fully double, star-shaped white florets age through green tints to a soft pink blush as summer progresses.

directions: Wedding Gown is a reblooming lacecap hydrangea whose fully double, ruffled white florets give a fuller, more textured look than typical single-flowered lacecaps, opening pure white before aging through pale green and eventually a light pink blush late in the season. It flowers on both old and new wood, so a late freeze that damages overwintered buds still leaves a strong summer and fall display. Because the double white blooms lack the pigment response to soil aluminum, their color stays fairly stable regardless of soil pH, unlike blue-to-pink shifting mopheads. Keep soil evenly moist and humus-rich in morning sun with afternoon shade, and prune only to remove dead wood immediately after the first flush so as not to sacrifice old-wood buds.
